A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JLDE research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on node classification, uncertainty estimation, calibration, runtime, and synthetic graphs in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables, ablations, and synthetic homophily experiment in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The post-hoc JLDE procedure remains unchanged: KNN density estimation using concatenated MPNN representations, with the same PCA reduction and Algorithm 1 implementation (Section 4.4; Appendix C).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Roman Empire, Amazon Ratings, Chameleon, Squirrel, CoraML, and PubMed under the same leave-out-class and near/far feature shifts. The synthetic graph coverage in Appendix E.5 is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines, including GPN, SGCN, BGCN, GPRGNN, FSGNN, FAGCN, ensembles, MCD, EBM, Safe, and GEBM. Table 17 retains the same KNN, MoG, and KDE comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–E retain the same data preparation, distribution-shift construction, backbone configurations, hyperparameter search, optimization, stopping rules, and evaluation metrics. No experimental setting or evaluation procedure is revised.

E4.justification: The layer-combination and backbone ablations, varying-homophily experiment, confidence-versus-accuracy analysis, runtime comparison, and density-estimator ablation are unchanged (Figures 4 and 6–10; Tables 6 and 17).

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10 dataset splits with 10 model initializations each and report the same standard deviations. The runtime comparison still averages over 25 runs (Table 6); uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, rankings, and plotted findings match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains JLDE's Roman Empire epistemic AUC-ROC values of 76.9, 93.8, and 100.0 for leave-out-class, near-feature, and far-feature shifts, respectively.

T1.justification: The information-theoretic definitions, Theorem 4.1, Propositions 4.1–4.2 and A.1, and their Appendix A proofs are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions or derivations are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: an information-theoretic analysis motivating JLDE, strong uncertainty estimation on heterophilic graphs, and competitiveness on homophilic graphs.

C2.justification: The explanations linking heterophily to complementary layer information are unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same qualifications concerning aleatoric uncertainty, calibration, classification-focused evaluation, and KNN scalability.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation details, PCA variance threshold, k=5, hyperparameters, software, and hardware information. The code-access information is unchanged; the new funding acknowledgement adds no technical reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Section 3, Appendix B, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. Bibliographic entries move across pages because of the acknowledgement insertion, without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgements section between the conclusion and Impact Statement, replaces 12 appendix cross-reference labels with 'Section', and updates the arXiv version/date marking. The scientific prose and existing section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement insertion shifts the Impact Statement and reference layout on pages 9–12, and cross-reference edits cause local line reflow. Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–17 retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and makes small cross-reference and layout edits. Its scientific reasoning, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so these editorial updates do not materially alter overall paper quality.
